transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm not wasting your time with this, but... I guess I've just been having a little trouble lately. 

I've noticed that I keep sort of... dodging anything that even remotely reminds me of my old job. Like, I'll completely avoid certain office buildings, or I'll skip security talks, or... even networking events if they're anywhere near the old work sites. I just tell people I'm too busy, which isn't completely a lie, I guess? But, um... if anyone starts asking questions about... about the day it happened, I just make up a polite excuse and get out of there as fast as I can. 

I know it's probably silly of me to act like that, and I really don't want to be difficult or make things awkward for anyone, but... is that the sort of thing you can help with? Does that make sense?
Can you tell me more about the day you're referring to? Was there a specific event that happened at your old job that has been particularly upsetting or traumatic for you?

Oh, um... well, I really don't want to make a big deal out of it. I know you probably see people who have been through much, much worse things, so I hope I'm not sounding dramatic or anything. 

It was just... a very bad day at work. An incident, I guess you could call it. Things just went very wrong on site, and... well, it was a lot to handle. I'm sorry, I'd actually prefer not to get into the exact details of what happened just yet, if that's okay with you? I just... I get a little flustered when I try to explain it, and I really don't want to break down and make things difficult for you right now. 

Is it alright if we just say it was a really difficult situation for now? I hope that's enough information... am I giving you what you need?
Since that difficult day at work, have you had any thoughts or mental images about it that keep coming back, even when you don't want them to?

Um... yes. I try really hard to just focus on the present, I really do, because I know I should be moving on. But... sometimes, out of nowhere, I'll just be doing something completely ordinary. Like, um, washing the dishes, or maybe driving past a warehouse gate. And suddenly the whole scene just... pops right back into my head. 

It's so sharp, I can actually hear the panic in people's voices all over again, and my chest gets all tight, almost like I'm right back there. I always try to shake it off right away so I don't make a fuss or let it ruin the day, but... it does happen. Is... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Since that day, have you found yourself avoiding other situations, places, or activities that you used to be comfortable with, even ones that aren’t related to your old job?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I really try my best to keep up with everything else in my life, you know? I still go to the grocery store, and run my normal errands, and do things with my family. I really don't want to be a burden on anyone or make them change their plans just because I'm feeling a little... off. 

So, it's really just those specific work-related things I mentioned earlier that I tend to steer clear of. I try to just push through everything else so I don't cause any trouble. I hope that's okay? I just haven't really noticed myself hiding from everyday things... am I answering that the way you need me to?
Since that day, have you noticed any changes in the way you feel or think about yourself or the world, like feeling guilty, blaming yourself, or losing interest in things you used to care about?

Well, um... I try really hard to keep a positive outlook, I really do. I don't want to be a cynical person, and I know most people are good. But... I guess I have noticed a little bit of a change in how I view others lately. 

I hope it doesn't make me sound awful, but... since then, I just catch myself thinking that maybe nobody is really safe to trust. Which I know probably sounds terrible! It's just... well, when someone you managed, someone you really tried to help and do the right thing for, can just turn around and become so dangerous... it just shakes your faith a little bit. 

I really try to push those thoughts away as soon as they happen because I don't want you to think I'm paranoid or bitter or anything like that. I'm trying my best to get past it. Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question the right way.
Since that day, have you noticed yourself feeling more angry, guilty, or sad than usual, even when you're not thinking about the incident?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I try very hard to keep my spirits up. I don't want to be one of those people who just walks around angry or feeling sorry for themselves, you know? I really try to be pleasant and keep things normal for everyone around me. 

I know some people get really down or irritable after something bad happens, but I just... I try to brush it off and keep smiling. I don't think I've been walking around feeling sad or guilty or anything like that out of the blue. I really hope I'm not coming across as difficult, but I just haven't really noticed those kinds of feelings. Is it okay that I don't have that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Since that day, have you noticed any ongoing feelings of fear, anger, or guilt—even when you're not actively thinking about the incident?

Oh, I'm sorry, did I not explain that well just a moment ago? I know you just asked something very similar, so I hope I didn't answer it wrong before. 

But, um, no... honestly, I really don't have this constant fear or anger hanging over me. I pride myself on keeping a level head. When you've managed as many operations and people as I have over the years, you really have to learn to keep your emotions in check, you know? So I just don't let myself walk around feeling mad or scared when I'm just going about my day. 

I really hope I'm not messing up your assessment by not having those symptoms? I know you're looking for certain things, and I really am trying to be as helpful as I can. I just haven't noticed those feelings lingering like that.
How long have these symptoms been going on since that difficult day at work?

Well, um... it's been a while now. I guess it started right after they let me go following the, um, the incident with the weapon. That was about a year and seven months ago. 

I know that probably sounds like a long time to still be dealing with things, and I really hope you don't think I'm just dwelling on the past or not trying hard enough to move on. I really have been trying my best to push through it. Does... does that timeframe make sense for what you usually see? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right details.
Since that day, have you found yourself being more on edge or easily startled, even in situations that didn't used to bother you?

Um... well, I guess maybe a little bit? I feel kind of silly admitting it, to be honest. I really don't want to sound like a nervous wreck or anything, because I've always been the steady one at work. 

But... yeah, if a car backfires outside, or even if just a heavy door slams, I jump. Like, really hard. And if somebody touches my shoulder when I don’t see them coming, I practically leap out of my skin. My heart just starts pounding, and it keeps racing long after everyone else has just moved on and forgotten about it. 

I try my best to hide it, of course, so I don't make anyone else uncomfortable or seem dramatic. I hope that doesn't make me sound too fragile... is that the kind of thing you mean? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right.
Can you tell me if you’ve had any moments where you felt intense fear, horror, or helplessness connected to memories of the incident at work?

Well, um... no, I don't think so. I really hope I'm not frustrating you by saying no again. I know you're being so thorough, and I really appreciate it, and I want to be as helpful as possible. 

But... when I think back on what happened, I don't really get overwhelmed by horror or, um, helplessness. Like I was saying before, as a manager, I've always been the one in charge of fixing things, so feeling helpless just isn't something I really let myself do. I just try to look at the memory logically and not let my emotions get the better of me. 

Is... is it okay that I don't feel that way? I know you're probably looking for a specific pattern, and I just want to be sure I'm answering you properly and giving you what you need.
